XII.|OF THE APOSTLES.|325}}</noinclude>intermission vnto God for him. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=6}}† And vvhen Herod vvould haue brought him forth, the same night Peter vvas sleeping betwene two souldiars, bound vvith {{sup|‖}} tvvo chaines: and the keepers before the doore kept the prison. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=7}}† And behold an Angel of our Lord stoode in presence: and light shined in the house: and striking Peters side, he raised him, saying, Arise quickely. And the chaines fel from his handes. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=8}}† And the Angel said to him, Gird thee, and put on thy shoes. And he did so. And he said to him, Put thy garment about thee, & folovv me. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=9}}† And going forth he folovved him, & he knew not that it vvas true vvhich vvas done by the Angel: but he thought that he savv a vision. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=10}}† And passing through the first & the second vvatch, they came to the yron gate that leadeth to the citie, vvhich of it self opened to them. And going out, they vvent forvvard one streate: and incontinent the Angel departed from him. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=11}}† And Peter returning to him self, said: Novv I know in very deede that our Lord hath sent his Angel, and deliuered me out of Herods hand, & from al the expectation of the people of the Iewes.⊣

{{verse|chapter=12|verse=12}}† And considering, he came to the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ It is much for the praise of these good Christians that the assemble to Gods seruice & praier was kept in their houses in the time of persecution, & that the Apostle came thither straight out of prison, as his first refuge. as now Christian people doe much to their commendation, in places where Heresie doth reigne.}}∷ house of Marie the mother of Iohn, who vvas surnamed Marke, vvhere many were gathered and praying. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=13}}† And when he knocked at the doore of the gate, there came forth a vvenche to see, named Rhodè. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=14}}† And as she knew Peters voice, for ioy she opened not the gate, but running in she told that Peter stoode before the gate. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=15}}† But they said to her, Thou art mad. But she affirmed that it vvas so. But they said, It is {{sup|‖}} his Angel. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=16}}† And Peter continued knocking. And when they had opened, they savv him, & were astonied. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=17}}† And beckening with his hand to them, that they should hold their peace, he told hovv our Lord had brought him out of prison, and he said, {{sup|‖}} Tel these things to Iames & to the brethren. And going forth he vvent {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Though God had so miraculously deliuered him, yet he would not tempt God by tarying among his persecutors, but according to Christes commaundement fled for a time.}}∷ into an other place. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=18}}† And when day vvas come, there vvas no litle a doe betvvene the souldiars, vvhat vvas become of Peter. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=19}}† And Herod, vvhen he had sought him, and had not found, making inquisition of the keepers, commaunded them to be led away: & going dovvne from Iewrie into Cæsaréa, there he abode. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=20}}† And he vvas angrie vvith the Tyrians and the Sidonians. But they vvith one accord came to him, and persuading Blastus that vvas cheefe of the kings chamber, they desired peace, for that their countries vvere nourished by him. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=21}}† And vpon<noinclude>{{rh||Ss iij|a}}</noinclude>
